content: 1. To reduce the dropout rates between DTP1 and DTP3, as well as BCG and MCV1, to less than 10% in all districts by 2018, micro-planning workshops should be conducted in 100% of identified high-risk communities. 2. To address immunization equity, the percentage gap in DTP3 coverage between the highest and lowest socio-economic quintiles should be reduced to 20% by 2018. This requires implementing and monitoring a plan to reach all areas at least four times a year. 3. For the introduction of new vaccines, the goal is to achieve over 90% coverage of the HPV vaccine for 14-year-old girls by 2018. This involves introducing the HPV vaccine through school-based programs into the national schedule by 2015 and ensuring its provision to all females aged 12 to 13 years through school programs. 4. An HPV immunization catch-up program should be implemented for all young girls aged 15–18, and cervical cancer screening should be extended to 100% of districts by 2018. 5. A national HPV register should be established to collect data for evaluating the impact of the HPV vaccination program on HPV-related cancer rates. This register should also facilitate reminders and follow-up systems for incomplete vaccinations. 6. Immunization program management objectives should focus on areas such as political commitment, policy, legislation, regulation, standard operating procedures, private sector partnerships, and monitoring and evaluation plans. 7. Human resource management objectives should include staff production and mix, placement and retention, workforce motivation, and human resource development. These should align with broader health-sector strategies. 8. Financial planning objectives should address financing, resource mobilization, efficiency, sustainability, financial management, and procurement. These should be linked to the health-sector financing strategy. 9. Vaccine and logistics management should focus on vaccine management, cold-chain systems, transport and infrastructure, injection safety, and waste management. Planners should refer to global criteria for effective vaccine management. 10. Monitoring, surveillance, and reporting have become increasingly important due to disease elimination targets and the introduction of new vaccines. Objectives should include routine reporting, surveillance, data quality assessments, immunization safety, and operational research. 11. Demand generation and communication strategies should emphasize the value of vaccines and the right to access immunization services. This includes communication strategies, health education materials, motivational strategies, and partnerships with communities and civil society organizations. 12. The cMYP (comprehensive Multi-Year Plan) should align with national, regional, and global immunization and health-sector strategies. This ensures stronger alignment and identifies overlooked strategies. 13. A national monitoring and evaluation framework should track progress toward cMYP goals and enable adjustments to strategies if milestones are not achieved. This framework should demonstrate clear linkages from inputs and activities to system outputs, coverage outcomes, and health impacts. 14. Logical frameworks for health system strengthening should be adapted for immunization programs, promoting alignment with broader health-sector frameworks. 15. Inputs and activities should include financial and human resource investments, health outreach programs, and immunization campaigns. Indicators should measure whether planned activities and resource commitments have been implemented. 16. System outputs should reflect the readiness of immunization and health systems to deliver services, such as cold-chain functionality and vaccine stock availability. 17. Immunization outcomes should measure program reach and coverage, including coverage rates, dropout rates, and equity indicators. 18. The ultimate impact of immunization programs should be measured in terms of reductions in morbidity, disability, mortality, and vaccine-preventable disease incidence. Impact indicators should assess the attainment of overall cMYP goals.
